title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
text: plot_bootstrap_forest() visualises bootstrapped edge weights confidence intervals network estimated bootstrap_network() boot_glasso(). Three layouts available: plot_edge_diff_forest() visualises pairwise edge weight differences boot_glasso object. Four layouts: "linear", "circular", "chord", "tile".

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: net_tna  <- build_network(ai_coding, method = "relative") boot_tna <- bootstrap_network(net_tna, iter = 200, seed = 42)

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: plot_bootstrap_forest(boot_tna,   title    = "Human-AI interaction in coding",   subtitle = "95% bootstrap CI  |  200 iterations")

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: plot_bootstrap_forest(boot_tna, layout = "circular",   title = "Human-AI Interaction Network — Circular")

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: plot_bootstrap_forest(boot_tna, layout = "grouped",   title = "Human-AI Interaction — Grouped by Source Node")

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: net_srl  <- build_network(srl_strategies, method = "glasso") boot_srl <- boot_glasso(net_srl, iter = 200, seed = 42)

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: plot_bootstrap_forest(boot_srl,   title = "SRL Strategies — Partial Correlation Network")

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
text: Compare whether pairs edges significantly different weights.

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
code: plot_edge_diff_forest(boot_srl, layout = "tile",   title = "Edge Differences — Tile")

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots

title: Bootstrap Forest Plots
text: Compare bootstrap CIs across groups one plot.
code: nets_grp  <- build_network(group_regulation_long,   method = "relative", actor = "Actor",   action = "Action",  time  = "Time",   group  = "Achiever") boots_grp <- bootstrap_network(nets_grp, iter = 200, seed = 42) plot_bootstrap_forest(boots_grp,   title    = "Group Regulation — High vs Low Achievers",   subtitle = "95% bootstrap CI  |  200 iterations per group")

title: Visualization of communities and hyper order networks
text: cograph provides two functions visualizing community structure higher-order relationships networks: overlay_communities() — renders network splot() overlays smooth blob shapes highlighting communities plot_simplicial() — visualizes higher-order pathways (simplicial complexes) blobs ggplot2 canvas accept network type: tna, matrix, igraph, cograph_network. use TNA model collaborative group regulation throughout:
code: model <- tna(group_regulation)

title: Visualization of communities and hyper order networks
text: simplest way: pass igraph community detection method name. Partial matching flexible naming supported.  igraph cluster_* method works: "walktrap", "louvain", "fast_greedy", "leading_eigen", "infomap", "leiden", "label_prop", "edge_betweenness", "spinglass", "optimal", "fluid_communities". can use full igraph name ("cluster_walktrap"), short name ("walktrap"), partial match ("leading_eige"). Directed graphs automatically converted undirected detection.  Define communities manually named list:  numeric vector factor position maps node:   Communities can share nodes:
code: overlay_communities(model, "fast_greedy") overlay_communities(model, "louvain") overlay_communities(model, list(   Regulatory = c("plan", "monitor", "adapt"),   Social     = c("cohesion", "emotion", "consensus"),   Task       = c("discuss", "synthesis", "coregulate") )) overlay_communities(model, c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3)) overlay_communities(model, "louvain", blob_colors = c("#E5B000", "#B4D7E0", "#C5E8A4")) overlay_communities(model, list(   "Self-Regulation" = c("plan", "monitor", "adapt", "emotion"),   Collaboration     = c("cohesion", "consensus", "discuss",                          "coregulate", "synthesis") ), blob_colors = c("#4FC3F7", "#fbb550"), blob_alpha = 0.30)

title: Multi-Cluster Multi-Level Visualization with plot_mcml: A Complete Guide
text: Large networks many nodes multiple constructs, components, factors fundamental problem hard work . Consider network 20 nodes, representing construct: motivation, engagement, emotions, collaboration. network 400 possible connections way one can make sense . common solution concatenate nodes lose internal relations, plot 400 edges get lost details. Multi-Cluster Multi-Level network (MCML, despite long name) designed solve problem. works creating network within cluster showing connections summarizing inter-cluster connections macro-level network. way, preserve data integrity value fine-grained details. Think MCML network networks. MCML workflow critical analytical advantage: built, macro network cluster network full TNA networks right. means can compute centrality, run bootstrap stability analysis, permutation tests, even higher-order pathway analysis (HYPA) cluster independently. MCML just visualization — decomposition complex network interpretable, analyzable sub-networks. Installation cograph Nestimate CRAN. Nestimate handles MCML computation (build_mcml, as_tna); cograph handles visualization (plot_mcml, splot).
code: #install.packages("cograph") #install.packages("Nestimate")

title: Multi-Cluster Multi-Level Visualization with plot_mcml: A Complete Guide
text: use human_long dataset bundled Nestimate — 10,796 coded human actions 429 human-AI programming sessions. coding scheme 9 codes grouped 3 clusters — codes become nodes, clusters become groups. plot_mcml() models levels simultaneously single figure. bottom layer shows every node inside cluster full edges drawn cluster level. top layer collapses cluster single macro-level node, edges carrying aggregated inter-cluster flow. Dashed inter-layer lines connect node cluster’s macro node, making hierarchical mapping explicit. Directive — human telling AI (commanding, specifying requirements, requesting) Evaluative — human judging AI output (correcting, expressing frustration, refining, verifying) Metacognitive — human stepping back think redirect (inquiring, interrupting) Figure 1: MCML: cluster networks , macro network Clusters can defined three ways. produce result: Named list (common): Data frame node group columns: Extracted data grouping variable already exists: Clusters Come ? Theory: Define groups based domain knowledge, . Community detection: Use detect_communities() cograph discover structure algorithmically. External grouping variables: nodes metadata (e.g., department, brain region, country), use . as_tna() converts MCML individual networks — macro network one network per cluster: element full TNA network can plotted, analyzed, bootstrapped independently: Figure 2: MCML decomposed individual networks: macro + cluster
code: data("human_long", package = "Nestimate")  net <- build_network(   human_long,   actor = "session_id", action = "code", time = "timestamp",   method = "relative" )  clusters <- list(   Directive     = c("Specify", "Command", "Request"),   Evaluative    = c("Verify", "Frustrate", "Correct", "Refine"),   Metacognitive = c("Interrupt", "Inquire") )  mcml_obj <- Nestimate::build_mcml(net, clusters, type = "tna") mcml_obj MCML Network ============ Type: tna  | Method: sum Nodes: 9  | Clusters: 3 Transitions: 10270   Macro: 5188  | Per-cluster: 5082  Clusters:   Directive (3): Specify, Command, Request   Evaluative (4): Verify, Frustrate, Correct, Refine   Metacognitive (2): Interrupt, Inquire  Macro (cluster-level) weights:               Directive Evaluative Metacognitive Directive        0.6056     0.2241        0.1703 Evaluative       0.4774     0.4057        0.1169 Metacognitive    0.4170     0.3275        0.2555 splot(mcml_obj) clusters <- list(   Directive     = c("Specify", "Command", "Request"),   Evaluative    = c("Verify", "Frustrate", "Correct", "Refine"),   Metacognitive = c("Interrupt", "Inquire") ) clusters_df <- data.frame(   node  = c("Specify", "Command", "Request",             "Verify", "Frustrate", "Correct", "Refine",             "Interrupt", "Inquire"),   group = c(rep("Directive", 3), rep("Evaluative", 4), rep("Metacognitive", 2)) ) clusters_auto <- split(human_long$code, human_long$cluster) |> lapply(unique) grp <- Nestimate::as_tna(mcml_obj) names(grp) [1] "macro"         "Directive"     "Evaluative"    "Metacognitive" splot(grp)

title: Multi-Cluster Multi-Level Visualization with plot_mcml: A Complete Guide
text: cluster assigned one color propagates consistently across every visual element: shell fill, node fill, within-cluster edges, pie-chart slice top layer, legend entry. colors NULL (default), colorblind-safe palette generated automatically. override , pass character vector one color per cluster, order cluster list. Choose colors sufficient contrast clusters — avoid hues similar. Muted, low-saturation palettes work well publication figures, saturated palettes effective slides posters: Figure 10: Custom cluster colors layers support four shapes: "circle" (default), "square", "diamond", "triangle". node_shape parameter controls detail nodes bottom layer, cluster_shape controls summary pie-chart nodes top layer. can single value (applied uniformly) vector length number nodes clusters, allowing per-element customization. Mixing shapes layers helps reader distinguish two levels glance. example , detail nodes use diamonds cluster’s summary node gets different shape: Figure 11: Diamond nodes mixed macro shapes Three size parameters control main visual elements independently. shape_size sets radius cluster’s elliptical shell bottom layer — increase nodes feel cramped inside shell. node_size controls individual detail nodes. summary_size controls pie-chart summary nodes top layer. Balancing three sizes determines visual hierarchy: large summary_size relative node_size draws reader’s eye macro level first, equalizing gives levels comparable visual weight: Figure 12: Larger shells nodes Cluster shells semi-transparent ellipses bottom layer visually group nodes. Two parameters control appearance: shell_alpha (fill transparency, 0–1) shell_border_width (border line width). Higher shell_alpha values create stronger visual grouping may obscure edges underneath; lower values keep shells subtle, letting network structure dominate. Increasing shell_border_width makes cluster boundaries prominent, helps shells overlap slightly: Figure 13: Thick borders, opaque shells Fine-tune borders layers independently. Detail nodes accept node_border_color; summary pie-chart nodes accept summary_border_color summary_border_width: Figure 14: Left: dark heavy borders; Right: colored borders matching clusters colored slice summary pie chart can represent two different quantities, controlled summary_pie: "inits" (default) — cluster’s share initial state distribution. Answers: “often sequences start cluster?” "self" — cluster’s self-retention ratio (self-loop weight / total -strength). Answers: “sticky cluster — much flow stays inside?” Figure 15: Left: initial state distribution; Right: self-retention ratio mostly-colored pie "inits" means cluster common starting point. "self", means cluster retains outgoing flow internally — transitions loop back rather escaping clusters. building macro network individual edges, aggregation parameter controls pairwise weights collapse cluster--cluster values: "sum" (default) — total flow volume. title: Network Estimation and Visualization with Nestimate + cograph
text: Nestimate unified network estimation package R. provides single entry point — build_network() — accepts sequence data, wide-format behavioral data, numeric matrices estimates networks using 10 built-methods. result netobject inherits cograph_network, every object produced Nestimate can plotted splot() directly. core design principle estimation visualization separate concerns: Nestimate handles computation (network construction, bootstrapping, permutation testing, clustering, multi-cluster analysis), cograph handles rendering. separation means analyst writes estimation code gets publication-ready figures without adapter code manual class conversion. Beyond single-network estimation, Nestimate provides complete statistical toolkit: Bootstrap stability analysis (bootstrap_network) — identifies edges survive resampling sampling artifacts. Permutation-based group comparison (permutation) — tests whether edges differ significantly conditions. Multi-cluster multi-level analysis (cluster_summary, build_mcml) — aggregates node-level networks cluster-level summaries hierarchical visualization. Centrality stability (centrality_stability) — assesses whether centrality rankings robust case dropping. Group-level operations — bootstrapping, permutation testing, plotting work grouped networks additional code. tutorial walks full pipeline group_regulation_long dataset shipped Nestimate.

title: Network Estimation and Visualization with Nestimate + cograph
text: common analytical question : given network individual states (nodes), can group meaningful clusters study clusters interact? MCML (Multi-Cluster Multi-Level) pipeline exactly . aggregates node-level network cluster-level summary, producing macro-level view (cluster--cluster transitions) per-cluster detail networks (within-cluster structure). several ways build MCML analysis, depending whether start pre-built network raw data, whether define clusters manually discover algorithmically. domain knowledge dictates grouping, define clusters named list node labels pass cluster_summary(). collaborative regulation, can distinguish regulatory behaviors (monitoring, planning, coregulating, adapting) social-communicative behaviors (cohesion, consensus, discussion, emotion, synthesis): splot() dispatches mcml object plot_mcml(), rendering two-layer visualization: bottom layer shows within-cluster detail networks, top layer shows macro (cluster--cluster) summary. title: Network Visualization with cograph: A Complete Plotting Guide
text: Network visualization R traditionally meant choosing two extremes: quick--dirty plots look like hairballs, heavily customized code takes longer write analysis . cograph collapses tradeoff. splot() function produces publication-ready network visualizations single call, sensible defaults can override parameter parameter. tutorial demonstrates everything single TNA model collaborative regulation behaviors. start zero-argument plot progressively layer customization — can see exactly parameter changes. plot — one line, zero arguments, publication-ready Node styling — shapes, colors, sizes, labels, centrality-based scaling Edge styling — width, color, curvature, labels, thresholds Donuts pies — composite node shapes multivariate data Themes palettes — pre-built visual themes Pipe-friendly API — sn_* function family chainable plot building Specialized plots — chord diagrams, heatmaps, alluvial flows Group comparisons — difference networks multi-group grids Bootstrap — validated network visualization Permutation testing — significant group differences Mixed networks — directed undirected edges combined TNA-specific workflows, see TNA tutorial. GitHub Development Version tutorial covers full feature set available GitHub development version cograph. CRAN release provides core plotting engine; development version adds themes, pipe API, specialized plots, additional features.
code: # Development version with full features # devtools::install_github("sonsoleslp/cograph") # CRAN version install.packages("cograph")

text: Overlay directed undirected edges plot. useful two types relationships — example, symmetric co-occurrence patterns asymmetric transition probabilities. defaults follow TNA conventions: oval layout, weight-scaled edges, dotted edge starts, visible edge labels. Figure 22: Co-occurrence (steel blue, straight) transitions (dark blue, curved) TNA-style defaults can distinguish edge types color: undirected co-occurrence edges straight steel-blue lines, directed transitions curved dark-blue arrows dotted starts. Edge widths scale automatically weight, stronger connections stand . Figure 23: Custom colors visually separate edge types
code: # Undirected: symmetric co-occurrence (half the weight for visual balance) set.seed(42) sym <- (model$weights + t(model$weights)) / 2 noise <- matrix(runif(length(sym), -0.02, 0.02), nrow = nrow(sym)) noise <- (noise + t(noise)) / 2  # keep symmetric diag(noise) <- 0 sym <- pmax(sym * 0.5 + noise, 0)  # Directed: original transition probabilities asym <- model$weights  # Defaults: oval layout, blue edges, weight-scaled widths, edge labels plot_mixed_network(sym, asym, threshold = 0.03,   title = "Co-occurrence + Transitions" ) plot_mixed_network(sym, asym, threshold = 0.03,   sym_color = "#E63946",   asym_color = "#003355",   title = "Red undirected + Blue directed" )

title: Higher-Order Network Analysis with Simplicial Complexes
text: methods analyze sequential pathways. Simplicial complex analysis takes different perspective: examines topological structure network . standard network captures pairwise relationships: node connects node B. many interactions involve groups: states , B, C may densely interconnected, forming triangle. simplicial complex formalizes : 0-simplex single node 1-simplex edge (two connected nodes) 2-simplex filled triangle (three mutually connected nodes) kk-simplex group k+1k+1 mutually connected nodes clique complex turns every clique simplex, lifting flat graph multi-dimensional topological object. f-vector (f0,f1,f2,…)(f_0, f_1, f_2, \ldots): counts simplices dimension. Betti numbers (β0,β1,β2,…)(\beta_0, \beta_1, \beta_2, \ldots): central invariants. β0\beta_0 = connected components, β1\beta_1 = independent loops, β2\beta_2 = enclosed voids. Euler characteristic χ=∑(−1)kfk=∑(−1)kβk\chi = \sum (-1)^k f_k = \sum (-1)^k \beta_k. contractible complex, χ=1\chi = 1. Simplicial degree: many higher-dimensional simplices node participates .  Nodes high simplicial degree topological hubs — participate many group interactions. captures group-level importance pairwise degree misses. single complex one threshold gives static snapshot. Persistent homology reveals topology evolves vary threshold. Start strongest edges progressively add weaker ones. Features persist across wide range topologically robust.  Betti curve (left): high threshold, network sparse (many components). threshold decreases, components merge (β0\beta_0 drops) loops may form (β1\beta_1 rises) get filled. Persistence diagram (right): Points far diagonal long lifetimes — structurally important features. Points near diagonal noise. Q-analysis (Atkin 1974) measures connectivity multiple levels structural sharing. Two maximal simplices q-connected share face dimension ≥q\geq q: q = 0: share least one node q = 1: share least one edge q = 2: share least one triangle  fragmentation point (first q components > 1) critical. , network fully connected shared sub-structures. , parts become structurally isolated. alternative clique complex: build simplicial complex pathways discovered HON — topology derived sequential dynamics rather network structure:  pathway complex, higher-order pathway becomes simplex. β0>1\beta_0 > 1 means states sequentially disconnected. β1>0\beta_1 > 0 means cyclic pathway structures. simplicial computations cross-validated igraph’s clique-finding verified via Euler-Poincaré theorem:

title: Introduction to cograph
text: R several network packages — igraph graph algorithms, qgraph psychometric networks, tidygraph dplyr-style manipulation. one thing well forces data format API. Going raw matrix filtered, annotated, publication-ready figure typically means loading three packages, converting formats, writing boilerplate code stitch results together. cograph designed eliminate friction. Every function — plotting, centrality, community detection, filtering — accepts major network format directly: matrices, edge lists, igraph, statnet, qgraph, tna objects. manual conversion. Centrality returns tidy data frame, list separate calls. Community detection one function 11 algorithms behind . Statistical annotations (confidence intervals, p-values, significance stars) render directly figure. need igraph statnet something cograph , to_igraph() to_network() convert back without data loss. Beyond standard network analysis, cograph visualizes higher-order sequential pathways simplicial blob diagrams, renders bootstrap stability results forest plots (linear, circular, grouped layouts), performs motif analysis identifies specific named node triples — just abstract type counts. result single package covers full workflow data import publication-ready output, remaining interoperable rest R network ecosystem.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 10 states <- c("Explore", "Plan", "Monitor", "Adapt", "Reflect",             "Discuss", "Synthesize", "Evaluate", "Create", "Share") mat <- matrix(0, n, n, dimnames = list(states, states)) # Sparse: ~30% of edges populated edges <- sample(which(row(mat) != col(mat)), 30) mat[edges] <- round(runif(30, 0.05, 0.5), 2)

title: Introduction to cograph
text: splot() main plotting function. One call, publication-ready output.  Key parameters: layout, minimum, node_fill, node_size, edge_labels, curvature, scale_nodes_by, theme, tna_styling. title: Migrating from qgraph to splot
text: splot() primary plotting engine cograph. renders network graphs using base R graphics designed work across wide range use cases: transition networks learning analytics, correlation networks psychology, social networks, weighted unweighted graph structure. accepts adjacency matrices, edge lists, igraph objects, tna objects, qgraph objects directly, fits existing workflows without requiring format conversion. function built useful every stage analysis. single call like splot(mat) produces clean, readable plot sensible defaults. need , function supports confidence interval underlays edges, significance stars derived p-values, templated edge labels combine estimates CI ranges stars (e.g., 0.25*** [0.12, 0.38]), pie donut charts nodes, publication-quality export 600 DPI. goal need switch tools analysis moves exploration final manuscript figure.

title: Migrating from qgraph to splot
text: One deliberate choices splot() consistent, predictable parameter naming system. Every parameter prefixed element controls – node_, edge_, label_, donut_, pie_, edge_label_, edge_ci_ – followed property: size, color, fill, width, alpha, . node_fill node fill color, edge_label_size edge label font size, donut_border_color donut border color, edge_ci_alpha confidence interval underlay transparency. naming designed learn pattern, can guess parameter names without checking documentation. contrasts conventions like vsize, posCol, border.width, label.cex, pieColor, every parameter follows different convention needs memorized individually.

title: Migrating from qgraph to splot
text: Network plots research often need communicate uncertainty significance alongside graph structure . splot() treats first-class concern rather afterthought. Edges can carry confidence interval underlays (edge_ci) – semi-transparent bands behind edge whose width reflects uncertainty estimate. Edge labels can built templates (edge_label_template) using placeholders like {est}, stars, {low}, {}, {range}, {p}, filled vectors CI bounds p-values supply. Significance stars computed automatically p-values edge_label_stars = TRUE. features mean single splot() call can produce network every edge shows weight, significance level, confidence interval – information otherwise require post-processing manual annotation.

code: model <- tna(group_regulation) splot(model) boot <- bootstrap(model, iter = 1000) splot(boot) model1 <- tna(group_regulation[1:1000,]) model2 <- tna(group_regulation[1001:2000,])  perm <- permutation_test(model1, model2, iter = 1000) splot(perm)

title: Why cograph?

title: Aggregate Duplicate Edges — aggregate_duplicate_edges
text: deduplicated data frame columns input, node pair appears aggregated weight.

title: Aggregate Duplicate Edges — aggregate_duplicate_edges
text: sum Total weight duplicate edges. Useful frequency counts edges represent additive quantities (e.g., number emails). mean Average weight. Useful averaging multiple measurements duplicates represent repeated observations. max Maximum weight. Useful finding strongest connection recent value. min Minimum weight. Useful conservative estimate earliest value. first Keep first occurrence. Useful preserving original order duplicates erroneous. output edge list uses canonical node ordering (lower index first undirected networks), ensuring consistent /assignment.

title: Degree Assortativity Coefficient — assortativity
text: degree assortativity coefficient defined Pearson correlation coefficient degrees nodes either end edge (Newman 2002): $$r = \frac{\sum_{jk} jk(e_{jk} - q_j q_k)}{\sigma_q^2}$$ \(e_{jk}\) fraction edges connecting degree-\(j\) degree-\(k\) vertices, \(q_k\) excess degree distribution, \(\sigma_q^2\) variance. directed networks, different degree combinations (/) source target ends can specified via type parameter.

One : "basic" (default) 6 canonical measures: degree, strength, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector, pagerank. "extended" Basic plus commonly-reported second-tier measures (~28 total): harmonic, coreness, eccentricity, radiality, lin, decay, load, stress, katz, alpha, power, authority, leverage, constraint, effective_size, bridging, transitivity, subgraph, diffusion, laplacian, kreach, current_flow_betweenness, current_flow_closeness. "" Every available measure (87). Passing measures explicitly overrides type. measures Character vector specific measure names compute. NULL (default) tier selected type used. Accepts "" shortcut every measure. custom vector valid measure names also accepted. Core (igraph-backed): "degree", "strength", "betweenness", "closeness", "eigenvector", "pagerank", "authority", "hub", "eccentricity", "coreness", "constraint", "transitivity", "harmonic", "alpha", "power", "subgraph". Native: "diffusion", "leverage", "kreach", "laplacian", "load", "current_flow_closeness", "current_flow_betweenness", "voterank", "percolation". Distance-based: "radiality", "lin", "decay", "residual_closeness", "dangalchev", "generalized_closeness", "harary", "average_distance", "barycenter", "wiener", "closeness_vitality". Spectral/walk: "communicability", "communicability_betweenness", "random_walk". Path-based: "stress", "flow_betweenness". Local/neighborhood: "lobby", "entropy", "semilocal", "clusterrank", "bottleneck", "centroid", "mnc", "dmnc", "lac", "topological_coefficient", "bridging", "local_bridging", "effective_size", "diversity", "cross_clique", "markov". Influence: "integration", "expected", "gilschmidt". Directed-: "salsa", "leaderrank", "trophic_level", "pairwisedis", "prestige_domain", "prestige_domain_proximity". Community-aware (require membership): "participation", "within_module_z", "gateway", "brokerage_coordinator", "brokerage_itinerant", "brokerage_representative", "brokerage_gatekeeper", "brokerage_liaison" (last 5 also require directed graph; see centrality_brokerage_coordinator). Zoo (batch 2): "gravity", "collective_influence", "local_hindex", "hindex_strength", "onion", "second_order", "infection", "nonbacktracking", "spanning_tree". Classical (batch 3, reference-validated): "katz" (Katz 1953), "hubbell" (Hubbell 1965), "information" (Stephenson-Zelen 1989), "reaching_local" (Mones et al. 2012). See centrality_katz, centrality_hubbell, centrality_information, centrality_pairwisedis, centrality_reaching_local. Psychometric (signed-weight): "expected_influence_1", "expected_influence_2" (Robinaugh, Millner & McNally 2016). Unlike strength (takes |w|), expected influence keeps sign — appropriate measure edges can negative (partial-correlation, glasso, signed correlation networks). mode directed networks: "", "", "". Similar eigenvector includes exogenous contribution power Bonacich power centrality - measures influence based connections influential nodes subgraph Subgraph centrality - participation closed loops/walks, weighting shorter loops heavily laplacian Laplacian centrality using Qi et al. (2012) local formula. Matches NetworkX centiserve::laplacian() load Load centrality - fraction shortest paths node, similar betweenness weights paths 1/count current_flow_closeness Information centrality - closeness based electrical current flow (requires connected graph) current_flow_betweenness Random walk betweenness - betweenness based current flow rather shortest paths (requires connected graph) voterank VoteRank - identifies influential spreaders via iterative voting mechanism. Returns normalized rank (1 = influential) percolation Percolation centrality - importance spreading processes. Uses node states (0-1) weight paths. states equal, equivalent betweenness. Useful epidemic/information spreading analysis. radiality Radiality centrality (centiserve). Sum (diam + 1 - d) normalized n-1. lin Lin's centrality. Reachable nodes squared divided sum distances. decay Decay centrality. Sum delta^d parameter delta. residual_closeness Residual closeness. Sum 1/2^d. dangalchev Dangalchev closeness (alias residual closeness). generalized_closeness Generalized closeness. Sum alpha^d. harary Harary centrality. Sum 1/d^2 reachable pairs. average_distance Average distance (centiserve). Sum distances / (n+1). barycenter Barycenter centrality. 1 / sum distances. wiener Wiener index. Total sum shortest path distances node. closeness_vitality Closeness vitality. Drop Wiener index node removed. communicability Total communicability. Row sums matrix exponential. communicability_betweenness Communicability betweenness. Fraction communicability node. random_walk Random walk centrality. Inverse sum random walk distances (requires connected graph). stress Stress centrality. Number shortest paths node. flow_betweenness Flow betweenness. Max-flow based betweenness. lobby Lobby index (h-index neighborhood). entropy Graph entropy centrality. Entropy change node removal. semilocal Semi-local centrality. Triple-nested neighborhood sum. clusterrank ClusterRank. Clustering coefficient times neighbor degree sum. bottleneck Bottleneck centrality. Count shortest path trees node critical. centroid Centroid value. Minimum f(v,) across nodes. mnc Maximum Neighborhood Component size. dmnc Density Maximum Neighborhood Component. topological_coefficient Topological coefficient. Shared neighbor ratio. bridging Bridging centrality. Betweenness times bridging coefficient. local_bridging Local bridging. (1/degree) times bridging coefficient. effective_size Burt's effective size. Degree minus redundancy. diversity Diversity centrality. Shannon entropy edge weight distribution. cross_clique Cross-clique connectivity. Count cliques containing node. markov Markov centrality. Inverse mean first passage time (requires connected graph). integration Integration centrality. Distance-based influence. expected Expected centrality. Sum neighbor degrees. gilschmidt Gil-Schmidt power index. Sum 1/d normalized n-1. salsa SALSA authority scores (directed graphs ). leaderrank LeaderRank. PageRank ground node (directed graphs ). participation Participation coefficient. Diversity inter-community connections (requires membership). within_module_z Within-module degree z-score. Intra-community connectivity (requires membership). gateway Gateway coefficient. Inter-community brokerage weighted centrality (requires membership).

Specific measures centrality(adj, measures = c("degree", "betweenness")) #>   node degree_all betweenness #> 1    A          2           0 #> 2    B          2           0 #> 3    C          2           0  # Directed network with normalization centrality(adj, mode = "in", normalized = TRUE) #>   node degree_in strength_in closeness_in betweenness eigenvector pagerank #> 1    A         1           1            1           0           1        1 #> 2    B         1           1            1           0           1        1 #> 3    C         1           1            1           0           1        1  # Sort by pagerank centrality(adj, sort_by = "pagerank", digits = 3) #>   node degree_all strength_all closeness_all betweenness eigenvector pagerank #> 1    A          2            2           0.5           0           1    0.333 #> 2    B          2            2           0.5           0           1    0.333 #> 3    C          2            2           0.5           0           1    0.333  # PageRank with custom damping centrality(adj, measures = "pagerank", damping = 0.9) #>   node  pagerank #> 1    A 0.3333333 #> 2    B 0.3333333 #> 3    C 0.3333333  # Harmonic centrality (better for disconnected graphs) centrality(adj, measures = "harmonic") #>   node harmonic_all #> 1    A            2 #> 2    B            2 #> 3    C            2  # Global transitivity centrality(adj, measures = "transitivity", transitivity_type = "global") #>   node transitivity #> 1    A            1 #> 2    B            1 #> 3    C            1

title: Domain Proximity Prestige — centrality_prestige_domain_proximity
text: sna's formula computes (counts > 0) * gdist element-wise sums get denominator. pair gdist = Inf (unreachable), R evaluates FALSE * Inf = NaN, entire denominator becomes NaN sna zeros every node via p[.nan(p)] <- 0. cograph masks .finite() summing, producing mathematically correct values directed graph, including disconnected components.

title: Local Reaching Centrality (Mones, Vicsek & Vicsek 2012) — centrality_reaching_local
text: Directed unweighted: \(LRC(v) = |\{u : u \ne v, v \u\}| / (N - 1)\). Undirected unweighted: average \(1/d(v, u)\) \(u \ne v\), divided \(N - 1\). Numerically equal igraph::harmonic_centrality(normalized = TRUE). Weighted: NetworkX convention, edge weights interpreted strengths path length \(\sum_e (\mathrm{total\_weight} / w_e)\). Per-path score mean original edge weights along shortest path. Bit-exact match networkx.local_reaching_centrality across three branches. Bit-exact match igraph::harmonic_centrality(normalized = TRUE) undirected unweighted branch. See reaching_global graph-level hierarchy measure derived per-node LRC.

title: Test Significance of Community Structure — cluster_significance
text: x Network input: adjacency matrix, igraph object, cograph_network. communities communities object (communities igraph) membership vector (integer vector communities[] community node ). n_random Number random networks generate null distribution. Default 100. method Null model type: "configuration" Preserves degree sequence (default). stringent test. "gnm" Erdos-Renyi model number edges. Tests random baseline. null null question answer. Default "detect": "detect" Null modularity best partition found community detection null graph. Answers "observed partition stronger community detection recover similar random graphs?" — historical behavior. "fixed" Null modularity supplied communities membership evaluated null graph. Answers "supplied partition explain structure similar random graphs?" — conservative test. seed Random seed reproducibility. Default NULL.

title: Test Significance of Community Structure — cluster_significance
text: cograph_cluster_significance object : observed_modularity Modularity input communities null_mean Mean modularity random networks null_sd Standard deviation null modularity z_score Standardized score: (observed - null_mean) / null_sd p_value One-sided p-value (probability observing equal higher modularity chance) null_values Vector modularity values null distribution method Null model method used null null question asked ("detect" "fixed") n_random Number random networks generated See cluster_significance.

title: Test Significance of Community Structure — cluster_significance
text: Two null models supported. default, null = "detect", generates n_random random networks, runs community detection (Louvain, fast-greedy fallback) , records resulting modularity. Low p-value means observed partition beats detection return similar random graphs. null = "fixed" instead evaluates user-supplied membership null graph, low p-value means partition stronger similar random graphs — tighter question isolates partition's quality detector's behavior. significant result (low p-value) indicates community structure stronger expected chance networks similar properties.

title: Test Significance of Community Structure — cluster_significance
text: Reichardt, J., & Bornholdt, S. (2006). Statistical mechanics community detection. Physical Review E, 74, 016110.

title: Cluster Summary Statistics — cluster_summary
text: x Network input. Accepts multiple formats: matrix Numeric adjacency/weight matrix. Row column names used node labels. Values represent edge weights (e.g., transition counts, co-occurrence frequencies, probabilities). cograph_network cograph network object. function extracts weight matrix x$weights converts via to_matrix(). Clusters can auto-detected node attributes. tna tna object tna package. Extracts x$weights. cluster_summary already cluster_summary, returns unchanged. clusters Cluster/group assignments nodes. Accepts multiple formats: NULL (default) Auto-detect cograph_network. Looks columns named 'clusters', 'cluster', 'groups', 'group' x$nodes. Throws error cluster column found. option works x cograph_network. vector Cluster membership node, order matrix rows/columns. Can numeric (1, 2, 3) character ("", "B"). Cluster names derived unique values. Example: c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3) assigns first two nodes cluster 1. data.frame data frame first column contains node names second column contains group/cluster names. Example: data.frame(node = c("", "B", "C"), group = c("G1", "G1", "G2")) named list Explicit mapping cluster names node labels. List names become cluster names, values character vectors node labels must match matrix row/column names. Example: list(Alpha = c("", "B"), Beta = c("C", "D")) method Aggregation method combining edge weights within/clusters. Controls multiple node--node edges summarized: "sum" (default) Sum edge weights. Best count data (e.g., transition frequencies). Preserves total flow. "mean" Average edge weight. Best cluster sizes differ want control size. Note: input already transition matrix (rows sum 1), "mean" avoids size bias. Example: cluster 5 nodes 5x weight cluster 1 node. "median" Median edge weight. Robust outliers. "max" Maximum edge weight. Captures strongest connection. "min" Minimum edge weight. Captures weakest connection. "density" Sum divided number possible edges. Normalizes cluster size combinations. "geomean" Geometric mean positive weights. Useful multiplicative processes. type Post-processing applied aggregated weights. Determines interpretation resulting matrices: "tna" (default) Row-normalize row sums 1. Creates transition probabilities suitable Markov chain analysis. Interpretation: "Given cluster , probability transitioning cluster B?" Required use tna package functions. Diagonal zero; per-cluster data $clusters. "raw" normalization. Returns aggregated counts/weights -. Use frequency analysis need raw counts. Compatible igraph's contract + simplify output. "cooccurrence" Symmetrize matrix: (+ t()) / 2. undirected co-occurrence analysis. "semi_markov" Row-normalize duration weighting. semi-Markov process analysis. directed Logical. TRUE (default), treat network directed. ->B B->separate edges. FALSE, edges undirected matrix symmetrized processing. compute_within Logical. TRUE (default), compute per-cluster transition matrices cluster. cluster gets n_i x n_i matrix showing internal node--node transitions. Set FALSE skip computation better performance macro (cluster-level) summary needed.

text: cograph's analytic functions follow single convention edge weights: Semantics. weight strength: higher weight means stronger connection (larger transition probability, thicker correlation, stronger tie). matches qgraph / tna convention intuition user-facing inputs. Path-based measures (betweenness, closeness, harmonic, eccentricity, stress, load, radiality, etc.) invert weights distances via 1 / weight ^ alpha. alpha argument (default 1) tunes strongly weight differences compress paths. Controlled invert_weights argument, auto-detects TRUE tna objects FALSE matrices/igraph (matching native igraph / sna defaults). Non-path measures (degree, strength, eigenvector, PageRank, transitivity, modularity, ...) use raw weights -without inversion. Unweighted override. Passing weights = NA analytic function forces unweighted behavior regardless attached graph. Individual functions may document exceptions help pages. deviation convention bug — please report.

title: Community Detection — communities
text: x Network input: matrix, igraph, network, cograph_network, tna object method Community detection algorithm. One : "louvain" - Louvain modularity optimization (default, fast) "leiden" - Leiden algorithm (improved Louvain) "fast_greedy" - Fast greedy modularity optimization "walktrap" - Random walk-based detection "infomap" - Information theoretic approach "label_propagation" - Label propagation (fast) "edge_betweenness" - Girvan-Newman algorithm "leading_eigenvector" - Leading eigenvector method "spinglass" - Spinglass simulation "optimal" - Exact modularity optimization (slow) "fluid" - Fluid communities algorithm community Optional integer character vector. supplied, returned data frame filtered rows whose community column matches one given values. Default NULL (keep communities). weights Edge weights. NULL, uses edge weights network available, otherwise unweighted. Set NA explicitly unweighted. resolution Resolution parameter modularity-based methods (louvain, leiden). Higher values yield communities. Default 1. directed Logical; whether treat network directed. Default NULL (auto-detect). seed Random seed reproducibility. applies stochastic algorithms (louvain, leiden, infomap, label_propagation, spinglass). ... Additional parameters passed specific algorithm. See individual functions details.

title: Detect Core-Periphery Structure — core_periphery

NULL (default), auto-detect matrix symmetry. Set TRUE force directed, FALSE force undirected. iter Integer; maximum number iterations continuous algorithm. Default 100. digits Integer NULL. Round numeric outputs many decimal places. Default NULL (rounding). ... Additional arguments passed to_igraph

title: Detect Core-Periphery Structure — core_periphery
text: list class "cograph_core_periphery" containing: scores Named numeric vector continuous coreness scores (0 = periphery, 1 = core) assignment Named character vector "core" "periphery" labels fitness Correlation adjacency matrix ideal core-periphery pattern core_density Edge density within core subgraph periphery_density Edge density within periphery subgraph

title: Detect Core-Periphery Structure — core_periphery
text: Continuous method (Borgatti-Everett): Finds coreness vector c (values 0-1) maximizes correlation adjacency matrix ideal rank-1 pattern matrix (outer product coreness vector ). algorithm initializes eigenvector centrality iteratively refines via power iteration convergence. Discrete method: Produces binary core (1) / periphery (0) assignment. Starts continuous solution, thresholds median, greedily swaps node assignments maximize fitness. Discrete fitness defined high density within core low density within periphery.

title: Detect Core-Periphery Structure — core_periphery
text: Borgatti, S.P. & Everett, M.G. (2000). Models core/periphery structures. Social Networks, 21(4), 375-395. doi:10.1016/S0378-8733(99)00019-2

title: Detect Core-Periphery Structure — core_periphery

title: Disparity Filter — disparity_filter
text: disparity filter identifies edges carry disproportionate fraction node's total weight, based null model weights distributed uniformly random. node \(\) degree \(k_i\), edge \((,j)\) normalized weight \(p_{ij} = w_{ij} / s_i\) (\(s_i\) node's strength), p-value : $$p = (1 - p_{ij})^{(k_i - 1)}$$ Edges significant \(p < level\) either endpoint.

title: Disparity Filter — disparity_filter

title: Dispersion (Backstrom-Kleinberg 2014) — dispersion
text: Let \(S_T = N(u) \cap N(v)\) mutual friends (embeddedness). Count pairs \((s, t) \subset S_T\) : \(s\) \(t\) directly connected, \(s\) \(t\) share common neighbor inside \(N(u)\) \(u\) \(v\). raw dispersion count. normalized = TRUE, result \((\mathrm{dispersion} + b)^{\alpha} /     (\mathrm{embeddedness} + c)\) (normalization skipped embeddedness + c == 0). Matches networkx.dispersion bit-exact three call modes (single pair, single source, full matrix).

title: Calculate Edge Centrality Measures — edge_centrality
code: # Create test network mat <- matrix(c(0,1,1,0, 1,0,1,1, 1,1,0,0, 0,1,0,0), 4, 4) rownames(mat) <- colnames(mat) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")  # All edge measures edge_centrality(mat) #>   from to weight betweenness overlap shared_neighbors triangles #> 1    A  B      1           2     0.5                1         1 #> 2    A  C      1           1     1.0                1         1 #> 3    B  C      1           2     0.5                1         1 #> 4    B  D      1           3     0.0                0         0  # Just betweenness edge_centrality(mat, measures = "betweenness") #>   from to betweenness #> 1    A  B           2 #> 2    A  C           1 #> 3    B  C           2 #> 4    B  D           3  # Sort by betweenness to find bridge edges edge_centrality(mat, sort_by = "betweenness") #>   from to weight betweenness overlap shared_neighbors triangles #> 1    B  D      1           3     0.0                0         0 #> 2    A  B      1           2     0.5                1         1 #> 3    B  C      1           2     0.5                1         1 #> 4    A  C      1           1     1.0                1         1 mat <- matrix(c(0,1,1,0, 1,0,1,1, 1,1,0,0, 0,1,0,0), 4, 4) rownames(mat) <- colnames(mat) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D") edge_betweenness(mat) #> A->B A->C B->C B->D  #>    2    1    2    3

what: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
text: Extract analyze triad motifs network data flexible filtering, pattern selection, statistical significance testing. Supports individual-level analysis (tna objects grouped data) aggregate analysis (matrices networks).

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
code: extract_motifs(   x = NULL,   data = NULL,   id = NULL,   level = NULL,   edge_method = c("any", "expected", "percent"),   edge_threshold = 1.5,   pattern = c("triangle", "network", "closed", "all"),   exclude_types = NULL,   include_types = NULL,   top = NULL,   by_type = FALSE,   min_transitions = 5,   significance = FALSE,   n_perm = 100,   seed = NULL )  # S3 method for class 'cograph_motif_analysis' print(x, n = 20, ...)

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
text: x Input data. Can : tna object (supports individual-level analysis) matrix (aggregate analysis , unless data id provided) cograph_network object igraph object data Optional data.frame containing transition data ID column individual-level analysis. Required columns: , , column(s) specified id. provided, x NULL matrix node labels. id Column name(s) identifying individuals/groups data. Can single string character vector multiple grouping columns. Required individual-level analysis non-tna inputs. level Analysis level: "individual" counts many people triad, "aggregate" analyzes summed/single network. Default depends input: "individual" tna id provided, "aggregate" otherwise. edge_method Method determining edge presence: "" Edge exists count > 0 (simple, recommended) "expected" Edge exists observed/expected >= threshold "percent" Edge exists edge/total >= threshold Default "". edge_threshold Threshold value "expected" "percent" methods. "expected", ratio (e.g., 1.5 means 50\ default 1.5 calibrated method. "percent", proportion (e.g., 0.15 15\ using "percent", set explicitly (e.g., 0.15). Ignored edge_method = "". Default 1.5. pattern Pattern filter triads include: "triangle" 3 node pairs must connected (direction). Types: 030C, 030T, 120C, 120D, 120U, 210, 300. Default. "network" Exclude simple sequential patterns (chains/single edges). Excludes: 003, 012, 021C. Includes stars triangles. "closed" Network without chain patterns. Excludes: 003, 012, 021C, 120C. Similar network also removes mutual+chain (120C). "" Include 16 MAN types, filtering. exclude_types Character vector MAN types explicitly exclude. Applied pattern filter. E.g., c("300") exclude cliques. include_types Character vector MAN types exclusively include. provided, types returned (overrides pattern/exclude). top Return top N results (observed count z-score). NULL returns results. Default NULL. by_type TRUE, group results MAN type output. Default FALSE. min_transitions individual level: minimum total transitions person included analysis. aggregate level: minimum triad weight count present. Default 5. significance Logical. Run permutation significance test? Default FALSE. n_perm Number permutations significance test. Default 100. seed Random seed reproducibility.

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
text: cograph_motif_analysis object (list) containing: results Data frame triad, type, observed count, (significance=TRUE) expected, z-score, p-value type_summary Summary counts motif type params List parameters used level Analysis level used

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
text: 16 triad types use MAN (Mutual-Asymmetric-Null) notation : First digit: number Mutual (bidirectional) pairs Second digit: number Asymmetric (one-way) pairs Third digit: number Null (edge) pairs Letter suffix: subtype variant (C=cycle, T=transitive, D=, U=)

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
text: Triangle patterns (pairs connected): 030C (cycle), 030T (feed-forward), 120C (regulated cycle), 120D (two -stars), 120U (two -stars), 210 (mutual+asymmetric), 300 (clique) Network patterns (structure): 021D (-star), 021U (-star), 102 (mutual pair), 111D (-star+mutual), 111U (-star+mutual), 201 (mutual+-star), plus triangle patterns Sequential patterns (chains): 012 (single edge), 021C (->B->C chain) Empty: 003 (edges)

title: Extract Motifs from Network Data — extract_motifs
code: # Small aggregate example -- no significance test for speed mat <- matrix(c(0,3,2,0, 0,0,5,1, 0,0,0,4, 2,0,0,0), 4, 4, byrow = TRUE) rownames(mat) <- colnames(mat) <- c("Plan","Execute","Monitor","Adapt") m <- extract_motifs(mat, significance = FALSE) print(m) #> Motif Analysis #> Pattern: triangle | Edge method: any #> Individuals: 1 | States: 4 | Total triads: 4 #>  #> Type distribution: #>  #> 030C 030T  #>    2    2  #>  #> Top 4 triads: #>                       triad type observed #> 1 Execute - Monitor - Adapt 030T        1 #> 2    Plan - Execute - Adapt 030C        1 #> 3  Plan - Execute - Monitor 030T        1 #> 4    Plan - Monitor - Adapt 030C        1  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ Mod <- tna::tna(tna::group_regulation) # Individual-level from tna -- keep n_perm tiny for example speed extract_motifs(Mod, top = 10, significance = TRUE, n_perm = 10L, seed = 1) # Filter to feed-forward loops only extract_motifs(Mod, include_types = "030T", significance = FALSE) } # }

Default NULL fits four. mode directed networks: "", "", "". Determines degree extract. Default "". directed Logical NULL. NULL (default), auto-detect matrix symmetry. Set TRUE force directed, FALSE force undirected. xmin Minimum degree include fitting. power-law, NULL triggers automatic estimation (Clauset et al. 2009 via igraph). distributions, NULL defaults 1. ... title: Fit Statistical Distributions to Degree Sequence — fit_degree_distribution
text: object class "cograph_degree_fit" containing: fits Named list, one entry per distribution, : distribution, parameters (named list fitted params), loglik, aic, bic, ks_stat, ks_p. comparison Data frame sorted AIC columns: distribution, aic, bic, ks_stat, ks_p. best Name best-fitting distribution (lowest AIC). degree degree vector used fitting.

title: Fit Statistical Distributions to Degree Sequence — fit_degree_distribution
text: Power-law (Pareto Type ): \(P(k) \sim k^{-\alpha}\). igraph available, uses igraph::fit_power_law() implementing Clauset et al. (2009) method. Otherwise, computes simple MLE: \(\alpha = 1 + n / \sum \log(k / k_{min})\). Exponential: \(P(k) \sim e^{-\lambda k}\). MLE: \(\lambda = 1 / \bar{k}\). Poisson: \(P(k) \sim \lambda^k e^{-\lambda} / k!\). MLE: \(\lambda = \bar{k}\). Note: KS test uses continuous approximation discrete distribution; p-values approximate. Geometric: \(P(k) \sim (1-p)^k p\). MLE: \(p = 1 / (1 + \bar{k})\).

title: Fit Statistical Distributions to Degree Sequence — fit_degree_distribution
text: Clauset, ., Shalizi, C. R., & Newman, M. E. J. (2009). Power-law distributions empirical data. SIAM Review, 51(4), 661–703.

title: Fit Statistical Distributions to Degree Sequence — fit_degree_distribution

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: Group centrality measures importance set nodes \(C \subseteq V\) rather single node. Three variants supported:

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
code: group_centrality(   x,   nodes,   measure = c("betweenness", "closeness", "degree"),   mode = c("all", "out", "in"),   normalized = TRUE )

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: x Network input (matrix, igraph, network, cograph_network, tna object). nodes Integer vector node indices (1-based) character vector node names identifying group \(C\). measure One "betweenness", "closeness", "degree". mode directed graphs measure = "degree": "" (directions), "" (outgoing), "" (incoming). Ignored undirected graphs measures. normalized Logical, "betweenness" . TRUE (default), divide \((|V| - |C|)(|V| - |C| - 1)\).

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: single numeric scalar — group centrality set nodes.

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: betweenness \(GBC(C) = \sum_{s,t \V \setminus C, s \ne t}     \sigma(s, t \mid C) / \sigma(s, t)\), \(\sigma(s, t)\) number shortest \(s\)-\(t\) paths \(\sigma(s, t \mid C)\) number paths passing least one node \(C\). Normalized \(1 / ((|V| - |C|)(|V| - |C| - 1))\). closeness \(GCC(C) = (|V| - |C|) / \sum_{v \V \setminus C}     d(v, C)\), \(d(v, C) = \min_{c \C} d(v, c)\) shortest distance \(v\) group member. Unreachable nodes contribute 0 denominator sum (matching NetworkX convention). directed graphs, cograph uses \(d(v, c)\) original direction, equivalent NetworkX's "reverse multi-source". degree \(GDC(C) = |N(C) \setminus C| / (|V| - |C|)\), fraction non-group nodes adjacent least one group member. mode = "" / "" pick corresponding directed neighborhood.

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: networkx.group_betweenness_centrality uses Puzis-Yahalom-Elovici iterative algorithm, produces results diverge textbook Everett-Borgatti / Puzis 2008 "least one node C" definition graph topologies (verified via independent Python brute-force). cograph implements textbook formula directly; group_closeness group_degree match NetworkX exactly.

title: Group Centrality (Everett-Borgatti 1999) — group_centrality
text: Everett, M. G., & Borgatti, S. P. (1999). centrality groups classes. Journal Mathematical Sociology, 23(3), 181-201. Puzis, R., Yahalom, R., & Elovici, Y. (2008). Augmentative data collection betweenness centrality. Advances Social Networks Analysis Mining (pp. 196-200). IEEE.

title: Fruchterman-Reingold Spring Layout — layout_spring
text: Compute node positions using Fruchterman-Reingold force-directed algorithm. Nodes connected edges attracted nodes repel .

title: Fruchterman-Reingold Spring Layout — layout_spring
code: layout_spring(   network,   iterations = 200,   cooling = 0.95,   repulsion = 1.5,   attraction = 1,   seed = NULL,   initial = NULL,   max_displacement = NULL,   anchor_strength = 0,   area = 1.5,   gravity = 0,   init = c("random", "circular"),   cooling_mode = c("exponential", "vcf", "linear"),   ... )

title: Fruchterman-Reingold Spring Layout — layout_spring
text: network CographNetwork object. iterations Number iterations (default: 200). cooling Rate temperature decrease exponential cooling (default: 0.95). repulsion Repulsion constant (default: 1.5). attraction Attraction constant (default: 1). seed Random seed reproducibility. initial Optional initial coordinates (matrix data frame). animations, pass previous frame's layout ensure smooth transitions. max_displacement Maximum distance node can move initial position (default: NULL = limit). Useful animations prevent large jumps frames. Values like 0.05-0.1 work well. anchor_strength Strength force pulling nodes toward initial positions (default: 0). Higher values (e.g., 0.5-2) keep nodes closer starting positions. applies initial provided. area Area parameter controlling node spread (default: 1.5). Higher values spread nodes apart. gravity Gravity force pulling nodes toward center (default: 0). Higher values (e.g., 0.5-2) prevent nodes drifting apart. init Initialization method: "random" (default) "circular". cooling_mode Cooling schedule: "exponential" (default, uses cooling parameter), "vcf" (Variable Cooling Factor - adapts based movement), "linear" (linear decrease iterations). ... Additional arguments (ignored).

code: motifs(   x,   named_nodes = FALSE,   actor = NULL,   window = NULL,   window_type = c("rolling", "tumbling"),   pattern = c("triangle", "network", "closed", "all"),   include = NULL,   exclude = NULL,   significance = TRUE,   n_perm = 1000L,   min_count = if (named_nodes) 5L else NULL,   edge_method = c("any", "expected", "percent"),   edge_threshold = 1.5,   min_transitions = 5,   top = NULL,   seed = NULL )  # S3 method for class 'cograph_motif_result' print(x, ...)  # S3 method for class 'cograph_motif_result' plot(   x,   type = c("triads", "types", "significance", "patterns"),   n = 15,   ncol = 5,   colors = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"),   ... )

title: Network Motif Analysis — motifs
text: x Input data: tna object, cograph_network, matrix, igraph, data.frame (edge list). named_nodes Logical. FALSE (default), performs census (type-level counts). TRUE, extracts specific node triples (instance-level). subgraphs() convenience wrapper sets TRUE. actor Character. Column name edge list metadata group . NULL (default), auto-detects standard column names (session_id, session, actor, user, participant). grouping column found, performs aggregate analysis. window Numeric. Window size windowed analysis. Splits actor's transitions windows size. NULL (default) means windowing. window_type Character. Window type: "rolling" (default) "tumbling". used window set. pattern MAN triad types include analysis: "triangle" (default) 7 closed triangle types: 030C, 030T, 120C, 120D, 120U, 210, 300. Excludes trivial open patterns (empty triads, single edges, chains, stars, mutual pairs). "network" types except trivially open ones. Excludes 003 (empty), 012 (single edge), 021C (chain). "closed" Like "network" also excludes 120C (mixed regulated). Excludes 003, 012, 021C, 120C. "" 16 MAN types, including empty trivial patterns. include Character vector MAN types include exclusively. Overrides pattern. exclude Character vector MAN types exclude. Applied pattern filter. significance Logical. Run permutation significance test? Default TRUE. n_perm Number permutations significance. Default 1000. min_count Minimum observed count include triad (instance mode ). Default 5 instances, NULL census. edge_method Method determining edge presence: "" (default), "expected", "percent". edge_threshold Threshold "expected" "percent" methods. Default 1.5. min_transitions Minimum total transitions unit included. Default 5. top Return top N results. NULL returns . seed Random seed reproducibility. ... Additional arguments passed internal plot helpers. type Plot type: "triads" Network diagrams specific node triples (instance mode) falls back patterns (census mode). Arranged grid. "types" Bar chart MAN type frequencies. "significance" Z-score plot showing - -represented types relative null model. Requires significance = TRUE motifs() call. "patterns" Abstract MAN pattern diagrams showing edge structure triad type. n Maximum number items plot. Default 15. ncol Number columns triad/pattern grid. Default 5. colors Two-element color vector: first color -represented positive values, second -represented negative values. Default c("#2166AC", "#B2182B") (blue/red).

title: Network Motif Analysis — motifs
text: cograph_motif_result object : results Data frame results. Census: type, count, (z, p, sig). Instances: triad, type, observed, (z, p, sig). type_summary Named counts MAN type level Analysis level: "individual" "aggregate" named_nodes Whether nodes identified (TRUE) exchangeable (FALSE) n_units Number units analyzed params List parameters used Invisibly returns input x.

title: Plot Multi-Cluster Multi-Layer Network — plot_mcml
text: Use plot_mcml need simultaneous micro/macro view cluster structure — bottom layer reveals internal cluster dynamics top layer provides bird's-eye summary. flat multi-cluster plot without summary layer, see plot_mtna. stacked multilevel/multiplex layers, see plot_mlna. Two workflows: Direct: pass weight matrix (tna / cograph_network object) together cluster_list. function calls cluster_summary internally compute aggregated weights. Pre-computed: call cluster_summary , inspect modify result, pass cluster_summary object x. avoids redundant computation plot clustering repeatedly different visual settings. Mode: "weights" (default) — displays raw aggregated edge values. Use absolute magnitude transitions matters. "tna" — row-normalizes summary matrix transition probabilities (rows sum 1) automatically enables edge labels layers (unless explicitly set edge_labels summary_edge_labels FALSE). Layout logic: Bottom-layer clusters arranged circle radius spacing, flattened perspective skew_angle. Nodes inside cluster sit smaller circle radius shape_size * node_radius_scale. top-layer summary nodes placed oval bottom layer whose proportions controlled top_layer_scale.

title: Plot Permutation Test Results — splot.tna_permutation
code: # Mock a tna_permutation object with synthetic data diffs <- matrix(c(0, .15, -.1, -.2, 0, .05, .1, -.05, 0), 3, 3) rownames(diffs) <- colnames(diffs) <- c("A", "B", "C") diffs_sig <- diffs; diffs_sig[abs(diffs) < 0.1] <- 0 perm <- list(edges = list(   diffs_true = diffs, diffs_sig = diffs_sig,   stats = data.frame(     edge_name   = c("A -> B","A -> C","B -> A","B -> C","C -> A","C -> B"),     diff_true   = c(.15,-.1,-.2,.05,.1,-.05),     effect_size = c(2.1,-1.5,-2.8,.4,1.2,-.3),     p_value     = c(.01,.04,.001,.3,.02,.5)))) attr(perm, "level")  <- 0.05 attr(perm, "labels") <- c("A", "B", "C") class(perm) <- c("tna_permutation", "list") plot_permutation(perm)

Default 1 uses full width. Use smaller values (e.g., 0.6) bring columns closer together. track_individuals Logical: draw individual lines instead aggregated flows? Default FALSE. TRUE, row data frame becomes separate line. line_alpha Alpha individual tracking lines. Default 0.3. line_width Width individual tracking lines. Default 0.5. jitter_amount Vertical jitter individual lines (0-1). Default 0.8. proportional_nodes Logical: size nodes proportionally counts? Default TRUE. node_label_format Format string node labels {state} {count} placeholders. Default NULL (plain state name). Example: "{state} (n={count})". bundle_size Controls line bundling large datasets. Default NULL (bundling). Integer >= 2: drawn line represents many cases. Numeric (0,1): reduce fraction original lines (e.g., 0.15 keeps 15 percent lines). bundle_legend Logical character: show annotation bundling active? Default TRUE shows "line ~ N cases" plot. Pass string use custom text ({n} placeholder count). bundle_legend_size Size bundle legend text. Default 3. bundle_legend_color Color bundle legend text. Default "grey50". bundle_legend_fontface Font face bundle legend text. Default "italic". bundle_legend_position Position bundle legend: "bottom" (default) "top".

what: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
text: Projects two-mode (bipartite/incidence) network one-mode adjacency matrix. Row-mode projection yields matrix shared-column connections among row nodes; column-mode projection converse.

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
code: project_bipartite(x, mode = "rows", method = "sum", ...)

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
text: x incidence matrix (rows = type 1 nodes, columns = type 2 nodes) non-zero entries indicate connections. Can also data.frame columns type1, type2, optionally weight. mode Character. "rows" (default) projects onto row nodes (result: n_rows x n_rows). "columns" projects onto column nodes (result: n_cols x n_cols). method Character. Projection method: "sum" Weighted projection: %*% t() (rows) t() %*% (columns). Edge weight equals sum shared connection weights. "binary" Co-occurrence count: binarize first, compute overlap. Edge weight equals number shared connections. "jaccard" Jaccard similarity: shared / (total_i + total_j - shared) pair. "cosine" Cosine similarity: dot product row (column) vectors divided product norms. "newman" Newman's weighted projection (Newman 2001): shared affiliation contributes 1 / (d_k - 1) d_k degree shared node. Gives weight connections exclusive affiliations. ... Additional arguments (currently unused).

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
text: square adjacency matrix row column names preserved input. Diagonal set 0 (self-loops).

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
text: Newman projection, affiliations shared one node focal type (d_k = 1) skipped, since 1 / (d_k - 1) undefined. follows convention Newman (2001).

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
text: Newman, M. E. J. (2001). Scientific collaboration networks. II. Shortest paths, weighted networks, centrality. Physical Review E, 64(1), 016132.

title: Project Bipartite Network to One-Mode — project_bipartite
code: # Incidence matrix: 4 students x 3 courses inc <- matrix(c(1, 1, 0,                 1, 0, 1,                 0, 1, 1,                 1, 1, 1), 4, 3, byrow = TRUE) rownames(inc) <- paste0("S", 1:4) colnames(inc) <- paste0("C", 1:3)  # Student co-enrollment (weighted) cograph::project_bipartite(inc, mode = "rows", method = "sum") #>    S1 S2 S3 S4 #> S1  0  1  1  2 #> S2  1  0  1  2 #> S3  1  1  0  2 #> S4  2  2  2  0  # Course overlap (Jaccard similarity) cograph::project_bipartite(inc, mode = "columns", method = "jaccard") #>     C1  C2  C3 #> C1 0.0 0.5 0.5 #> C2 0.5 0.0 0.5 #> C3 0.5 0.5 0.0  # Newman's weighted projection cograph::project_bipartite(inc, mode = "rows", method = "newman") #>     S1  S2  S3 S4 #> S1 0.0 0.5 0.5  1 #> S2 0.5 0.0 0.5  1 #> S3 0.5 0.5 0.0  1 #> S4 1.0 1.0 1.0  0

title: Rich Club Coefficient — rich_club

title: Rich Club Coefficient — rich_club
text: x Network input: matrix, igraph, network, cograph_network, tna object. rich Character. Prominence definition: "k" (degree, default) "s" (strength / weighted degree). weighted Logical. TRUE (default), compute weighted rich club coefficient. FALSE, compute unweighted version (density among rich nodes). normalized Logical. TRUE (default), normalize degree-preserving random graphs include confidence intervals. n_random Integer. Number random graphs normalization. Default 100. directed Logical NULL. Default NULL (auto-detect). seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. Default NULL. digits Integer NULL. Round numeric output. Default NULL. ... Additional arguments passed to_igraph.

title: Rich Club Coefficient — rich_club
text: data frame class "cograph_rich_club" columns: threshold, n_rich, phi, normalized: phi_norm, phi_rand, ci_lo, ci_hi.

title: Rich Club Coefficient — rich_club
text: Unweighted: \(\phi(k) = 2 E_{>k} / (N_{>k} (N_{>k} - 1))\) Weighted: \(\phi^w(k) = W_{>k} / \sum_{l=1}^{E_{>k}} w_l^{ranked}\) Normalization: \(\phi_{norm} = \phi_{obs} / \bar{\phi}_{rand}\). value > 1 indicates rich club ordering beyond degree sequence alone explains.

title: Rich Club Coefficient — rich_club
text: Opsahl, T., Colizza, V., Panzarasa, P. & Ramasco, J.J. (2008). Prominence control: weighted rich-club effect. Physical Review Letters, 101, 168702. Colizza, V., Flammini, ., Serrano, M.. & Vespignani, . (2006). Detecting rich-club ordering complex networks. Nature Physics, 2, 110-115.

title: Network Robustness Analysis — robustness
text: x Network input: matrix, igraph, network, cograph_network, tna object type Character string; either "vertex" "edge" removals. Default: "vertex" measure Character string; sort "betweenness", "degree", "random". Default: "betweenness" strategy Character string; "sequential" (default) recalculates centrality removal. "static" computes centrality original network removes nodes fixed order (brainGraph-style). affects targeted attacks; random removal unaffected. n_iter Integer; number iterations random analysis. Default: 1000 (matching brainGraph convention) mode directed networks: "", "", "". Default "". seed Random seed reproducibility. Default NULL. ... Additional arguments passed to_igraph

title: Network Robustness Analysis — robustness
text: data frame (class "cograph_robustness") columns: removed_pct Fraction vertices/edges removed (0 1) comp_size Size largest component removal comp_pct Ratio component size original maximum measure Attack strategy used type Type analysis (vertex edge removal)

title: Network Robustness Analysis — robustness
text: Three attack strategies available: Targeted Attack - Betweenness (default): Vertices/edges sorted betweenness centrality removed highest lowest. targets nodes bridge different network regions. Targeted Attack - Degree: Vertices sorted degree removed highest lowest. targets highly connected hub nodes. Note: edge attacks, degree available; use betweenness instead. Random Failure: Vertices/edges removed random order, averaged n_iter iterations. simulates random component failures. Strategy: strategy parameter controls targeted attacks work: "sequential" (default): Recalculates centrality removal. stronger attack removing hub changes nodes become new bridges/hubs. "static": Computes centrality original network removes nodes fixed order (brainGraph). matches original Albert et al. (2000) method. Scale-free networks typically robust random failures vulnerable targeted attacks, random networks degrade uniformly.

title: Network Robustness Analysis — robustness
text: Albert, R., Jeong, H., & Barabasi, .L. (2000). Error attack tolerance complex networks. Nature, 406, 378-381. doi:10.1038/35019019

title: Network Robustness Analysis — robustness

title: Set Edge Aesthetics — sn_edges
text: network cograph_network object, matrix, data.frame, igraph object. Matrices inputs auto-converted. width Edge width. Can single value, vector (per-edge), "weight". edge_size Base edge size weight scaling. NULL (default) uses adaptive sizing based network size: 15 * exp(-n_nodes/90) + 1. Larger values = thicker edges. esize Deprecated. Use edge_size instead. edge_width_range Output width range c(min, max) weight-based scaling. Default c(0.5, 4). Edges scaled fit within range. edge_scale_mode Scaling mode edge weights: "linear" (default), "log" (wide weight ranges), "sqrt" (moderate compression), "rank" (equal visual spacing). edge_cutoff Two-tier cutoff edge width scaling. NULL (default) = auto 75th percentile. 0 = disabled. Positive number = manual threshold. cut Deprecated. Use edge_cutoff instead. color Edge color. Can single color, vector, "weight" automatic coloring based edge weights. edge_positive_color Color positive edge weights. positive_color Deprecated. Use edge_positive_color instead. edge_negative_color Color negative edge weights. negative_color Deprecated. Use edge_negative_color instead. alpha Edge transparency (0-1). style Line style: "solid", "dashed", "dotted", "longdash", "twodash". curvature Edge curvature amount (0 = straight). arrow_size Size arrow heads directed networks. show_arrows Logical. Show arrows? Default TRUE directed networks. maximum Maximum edge weight scaling width. Weights capped. Similar qgraph's maximum parameter. width_scale Scale factor edge widths. Values > 1 make edges thicker, values < 1 make thinner. Applied width calculations. labels Edge labels. Can TRUE (show weights), vector, column name. label_size Edge label text size. label_color Edge label text color. label_position Position along edge (0 = source, 0.5 = middle, 1 = target). label_offset Perpendicular offset edge line. label_bg Background color edge labels (default "white"). Set NA transparent. label_bg_padding Padding around label text proportion text size (default 0.3). label_fontface Font face: "plain", "bold", "italic", "bold.italic" (default "plain"). label_border Border style: NULL (none), "rect", "rounded", "circle" (default NULL). label_border_color Border color label border (default "gray50"). label_underline Logical. Underline label text? (default FALSE). label_shadow Logical. Enable drop shadow labels? (default FALSE). label_shadow_color Color label shadow (default "gray40"). label_shadow_offset Offset distance shadow points (default 0.5). label_shadow_alpha Transparency shadow (0-1, default 0.5). bidirectional Logical. Show arrows ends edges? loop_rotation Angle radians self-loop direction (default: pi/2 = top). curve_shape Spline tension curved edges (-1 1, default: 0). curve_pivot Pivot position along edge curve control point (0-1, default: 0.5). curves Curve mode: FALSE (straight edges), "mutual" (curve reciprocal pairs), "force" (curve edges). Default FALSE. ci Numeric vector CI widths (0-1 scale). Larger values = uncertainty. ci_scale Width multiplier CI underlay thickness. Default 2. ci_alpha Transparency CI underlay (0-1). Default 0.15. ci_color CI underlay color. NA (default) uses main edge color. ci_style Line type CI underlay: 1=solid, 2=dashed, 3=dotted. Default 2. ci_arrows Logical: show arrows CI underlay? Default FALSE. ci_lower Numeric vector lower CI bounds labels. ci_upper Numeric vector upper CI bounds labels. label_style Preset style: "none", "estimate", "full", "range", "stars". label_template Template placeholders: {est}, {range}, {low}, {}, {p}, {stars}. label_digits Decimal places estimates template. Default 2. label_ci_format CI format: "bracket" [low, ] "dash" low-. label_p Numeric vector p-values edges. label_p_digits Decimal places p-values. Default 3. label_p_prefix Prefix p-values. Default "p=". label_stars Stars labels: character vector, TRUE (compute p), numeric (treated p-values).

text: Visualizes net_bootstrap objects Nestimate package. Mirrors splot.tna_bootstrap adapts Nestimate's field layout: weights live $original$weights, directed always TRUE, donut/inits. Plots original tna model nodes colored community membership. original model retrieved attr(x, "tna"), tna::communities() sets automatically. Uses walktrap present x$assignments; otherwise falls back first available algorithm column. Plots original network nodes colored community membership. network retrieved attr(x, "network"), detect_communities() / .wrap_communities() sets automatically. Applies TNA-compatible styling defaults delegating splot(): directed networks get oval layout, coloured nodes, sized arrows; undirected networks get spring layout arrows dashes. parameters can overridden caller. Visualizes boot_glasso objects Nestimate package. Plots partial-correlation network edge inclusion probabilities mapped edge transparency. Plot wtna_mixed object either single overlaid network two separate group panels. Visualizes net_permutation objects Nestimate package. Differs plot_permutation: p_values effect_size already p×p matrices (edge-name parsing needed), directed comes x$x$directed. Network visualization using base R graphics (similar qgraph). Creates network visualization using base R graphics functions (polygon, lines, xspline, etc.) instead grid graphics. provides better performance large networks uses snake_case parameter names soplot() consistency.

title: Node Vulnerability — vulnerability
text: x Network input: matrix, igraph, network, cograph_network, tna object. directed Logical NULL. NULL (default), auto-detect matrix symmetry. Set TRUE force directed, FALSE force undirected. normalized Logical. TRUE (default), return proportional drop. FALSE, return raw efficiency difference. weighted Logical. TRUE, honor edge weights computing shortest paths (Dijkstra); distance 1/weight^alpha per usual qgraph/tna convention invert_weights = TRUE. FALSE (default, matches prior behavior), edges treated unit length. invert_weights Logical. TRUE (default) weights present, invert weights distances via 1/weight^alpha higher weight = shorter path (matches centrality()'s default). Ignored weighted = FALSE. alpha Weight--distance exponent (default 1). digits Integer NULL. Round scores many decimal places. Default NULL (rounding). ... Additional arguments passed to_igraph.

title: Node Vulnerability — vulnerability
text: object class "cograph_vulnerability" components: scores Named numeric vector vulnerability scores, sorted descending. network original input network. normalized Logical flag indicating normalization mode.

title: Node Vulnerability — vulnerability
text: $$V() = \frac{E_{global} - E_{global \setminus }}{E_{global}}$$ \(E_{global}\) global efficiency full network \(E_{global \setminus }\) global efficiency removing node edges. Global efficiency defined : $$E_{global} = \frac{1}{n(n-1)} \sum_{\neq j} \frac{1}{d(,j)}$$ Nodes high vulnerability critical network's communication efficiency. Removing causes greatest drop global efficiency. Performance note: function computes -pairs shortest paths full graph per node removal, giving O(n) calls shortest-path algorithm. warning issued networks 500 nodes.

title: Node Vulnerability — vulnerability
text: Latora, V. & Marchiori, M. (2007). measure centrality based network efficiency. New Journal Physics, 9(6), 188. doi:10.1088/1367-2630/9/6/188
